why.A: Cultivate means to grow plants and care for them as they come up; you do not grow pollution back to its source.
why.B: Grant means to give or allow something formally; the scientists are following the pollution back to where it started, not handing anything out.
why.C: Commend means to praise someone or speak well of them, and pollution is being tracked here, not praised.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The city launched a public ______ to reduce litter in parks.
items.explanation: A campaign is an organized effort to achieve something, which is what a city launches against litter; a memoir, a canopy and a trance are not efforts.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A memoir is a book someone writes about their own life; a city cannot launch one at a litter problem.
why.C: A canopy is a cover overhead, either a cloth shade or the leafy roof of a forest; it is a thing, not an organized effort.
why.D: A trance is a dazed, half-asleep state; clearing litter from parks needs an organized plan, not a daze.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The company was accused of trying to ______ the facts to make its results appear better.
items.explanation: To distort is to twist facts out of shape, which is what making results “appear better” than they are does; to attain, soothe or conserve facts is not to bend them.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Attain means to reach or achieve something after working for it; facts are not something you reach, and the company is bending them.
why.C: Soothe means to take the sting out of something, the way cool water soothes a burn; facts cannot be soothed, and soothing anything is not dishonest.
why.D: Conserve means to save something carefully and not use it up, the way you conserve water; that is looking after something, not twisting it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Dark mountains appeared on the distant ______.
items.explanation: The horizon is the far line where land meets sky, which is where distant mountains appear; the midst is the middle of something, terrain is ground underfoot, a fringe is an edge.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: The midst of something is its middle, as in the midst of the crowd; mountains seen far off are at the furthest edge of what you can see, not in the middle of it.
why.C: Terrain means the land itself and the shape of it, such as rocky or hilly terrain; it is the ground you stand on, not the faraway line you see things against.
why.D: A fringe is the edge or border of a thing, like the fringe of a forest; what the sentence wants is the distant line where the land meets the sky.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A ______ student checks her work carefully and completes assignments consistently.
items.explanation: Diligent means steadily careful and hardworking, which is what checking work and finishing consistently shows; reckless, sluggish and aloof are the opposite habits.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Reckless means acting without caring about the danger or the consequences, which is the opposite of checking your work carefully.
why.C: Sluggish means slow and short of energy, like a slug; this student finishes her assignments steadily.
why.D: Aloof means keeping your distance from other people, cool and uninvolved; it describes how someone is with others, not how carefully she works.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The smell of pine trees can ______ memories of winter holidays.
items.explanation: To evoke is to call a memory or a feeling to mind, which is what a smell does; to confine, revoke or forbid a memory is not to summon it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Confine means to shut something in or keep it within limits; the smell is bringing memories to mind, not fencing them in.
why.B: Revoke means to take back something that was officially given; a memory was never given to you, and the smell is calling it up rather than withdrawing it.
why.C: Forbid means to order that something must not happen, and a smell cannot ban your memories.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The apartment was small but ______, with every inch used efficiently.
items.explanation: Compact means small but efficiently arranged, which is what using every inch means; plaintive, remote and ferocious describe nothing about space.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Plaintive means sounding or looking sad and mournful, like a plaintive cry; it describes sadness, not how a space is arranged.
why.B: Remote means far away from everything else, which is about where the apartment is, and the sentence is about how well the space inside it is used.
why.D: Ferocious means fierce and savage, the way a ferocious animal is; a small apartment is not fierce.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The agency decided to ______ the license after repeated safety violations.
items.explanation: To revoke is to cancel something already granted, which is what repeated safety violations cost a license; to acquire, commend or proclaim it is not to take it away.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Acquire means to get or obtain something; the agency is taking the license away after the violations, not getting one.
why.B: Commend means to praise someone or speak well of them, and repeated safety violations are not something an agency praises.
why.D: Proclaim means to announce something publicly and formally; after repeated safety violations the agency needs to take the license away, not read it out.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Early warnings helped ______ a larger disaster by giving residents time to leave.
items.explanation: To avert is to stop something bad before it happens, which is what early warnings and time to leave do; to dwindle, inundate or provoke a disaster is not to prevent it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Dwindle means to shrink away little by little, and things dwindle on their own; the warnings stopped the disaster rather than slowly shrinking it.
why.C: Inundate means to flood, the way a river inundates a field; flooding a disaster would make it worse, not stop it.
why.D: Provoke means to stir something up or deliberately bring it on; the warnings stopped the disaster instead of causing it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: After the article went viral, reporters ______ the scientist with questions.
items.explanation: To inundate is to flood, which is what a viral article does to a scientist with questions; to vacate, conserve or host someone is not to overwhelm them.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Vacate means to leave a place empty, as you vacate a room at the end of a stay; the reporters crowded in rather than clearing out.
why.C: Conserve means to save something carefully and not use it up, the way you conserve water; a person being asked questions is not being saved up.
why.D: Host means to be the one welcoming guests and looking after them; the reporters were not looking after the scientist, they were overwhelming her with questions.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: After the wildfire, the community center became a ______ for families who had lost their homes.
items.explanation: A sanctuary is a place of safety, which is what a community center becomes for families who have lost their homes; a verdict, a burden and a spectacle are not shelters.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A verdict is the decision reached at the end of a trial; it is a judgment, not somewhere families can stay.
why.B: A burden is a heavy load or a hard responsibility to carry; the community center is helping these families, not weighing them down.
why.C: A spectacle is a striking sight that people gather to watch; these families need somewhere safe, not something to look at.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Even after several failed attempts, the team continued to ______ for a better solution.
items.explanation: To strive is to keep trying hard, which is what continuing after several failed attempts is; to suspend, stifle or suspect a solution is not to go after it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Suspend means to hang something up, or to put it on hold for a while; the team kept going instead of stopping.
why.B: Stifle means to smother something or hold it back, like a fire stifled under a blanket; the team is chasing a better solution, not squashing one.
why.D: Suspect means to think something might be true without being sure, or to distrust someone; the team is searching for a solution, not doubting it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A junior assistant is ______ to the department manager.
items.explanation: Subordinate means lower in rank, which is what a junior assistant is to a manager; superior is the opposite, and unanimous and tangible are not about rank.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Unanimous means everyone in a group agrees about something, which says nothing about who ranks above whom.
why.C: Superior means higher in rank — but a junior assistant is the one below the manager, so this puts the relationship the wrong way round.
why.D: Tangible means solid enough to touch, and a person's rank is not something you can put your hand on.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: From the muddy footprints, I ______ that someone entered through the back door.
items.explanation: To infer is to work something out from the evidence, which is what muddy footprints let you do. The footprints imply it; the person reading them infers it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To imply is to hint at something without saying it, which is what the footprints are doing — the blank needs the word for what you do when you read the hint.
why.B: To suspend is to hang something up, like a lamp from a ceiling, and it has other meanings besides — but none of them is working something out from clues.
why.D: To trace is to follow a mark or a line along, and you can trace footprints. But you cannot trace that someone came in; the blank needs the word for the conclusion you reached.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The author never says the child is afraid, but the trembling hands ______ fear.
items.explanation: To imply is to suggest without stating, which is what trembling hands do about fear while the author says nothing. The reader infers; only the details imply.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To infer is to work something out from the clues, which is what the reader does here; the trembling hands are giving the hint, not drawing the conclusion.
why.B: To grant is to give or allow something officially, the way a school grants permission, and hands cannot grant anything.
why.C: Render means to make something become a certain way, as in 'the news rendered her speechless', which is not the same as quietly hinting at it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The statue remained ______, while the patient's condition remained stable.
items.explanation: Stationary means not moving, which is what a statue is. Stable, used of the patient in the same sentence, means steady rather than still — the sentence sets the two words side by side on purpose.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Rigorous means strict and exacting — a statue is not being strict about anything, it is simply not moving.
why.C: Subjective means based on personal feelings rather than facts, and a statue standing still is not anyone's opinion.
why.D: Remote means far away or out of the way, which is about where the statue is, not about it staying put.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A ______ training program is demanding and thorough.
items.explanation: Rigorous means demanding and thorough, which the sentence says outright; rigid means unbending, static means unchanging, whimsical means playful.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Whimsical means playful and full of odd little fancies, which is close to the opposite of demanding and thorough.
why.B: Rigid means stiff and unbending, so a rigid program is one that will not bend — the sentence is about how hard and thorough it is, not how inflexible.
why.C: Static means not changing, and a program could stay exactly the same year after year while still being easy.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The committee's decision was ______; every member voted yes.
items.explanation: Unanimous means everyone agreed, which is what “every member voted yes” says; remote, subjective and superior tell you nothing about agreement.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Remote means far away or out of the way, and how far off something is tells you nothing about whether the members agreed.
why.B: Subjective means based on personal feelings rather than the facts, and a decision could be subjective whether one member likes it or all of them do.
why.D: Superior means better, or higher in rank, but the sentence tells you everyone voted yes, which is about agreement rather than quality.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: She borrowed the first ______ of the encyclopaedia from the library.
items.explanation: A volume is one book of a set, and an encyclopaedia comes in numbered volumes.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: A charter is an official document setting out the rules or rights of a group, so it is not one of the books of an encyclopaedia.
why.C: Consensus means general agreement reached by a group, which is not a thing you can carry home from a library.
why.D: A trace is a tiny leftover sign that something was once there, far too small a word for a whole book.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: TANGIBLE most nearly means:
items.explanation: tangible: touchable, concrete, real — something you could actually hold or point at.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hopeful means full of hope, expecting something good, which is about how you feel rather than what you can touch.
why.C: Distant means far off, and something can be miles away and still be perfectly solid and touchable.
why.D: Imaginary means existing only in the mind, which is the opposite of tangible — a tangible thing is really there to hold.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The narrow mountain road became ______ after the ice storm.
items.explanation: Treacherous means dangerous and not to be trusted, which is what ice makes a narrow mountain road; rural, stable and spacious describe where the road is, not the danger.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Rural means out in the countryside, which this road may well be, but that says nothing about the ice or the danger.
why.B: Stable means steady and unlikely to shift or give way, and ice would make a road less stable, not more.
why.C: Spacious means roomy, with plenty of space, and the sentence has already called the road narrow.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The movement fought for women's ______, or the right to vote.
items.explanation: Suffrage is the right to vote, which the sentence defines outright with “or the right to vote”; consensus, a charter and prestige are not that right.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Consensus means general agreement in a group, and people can agree about something without anyone being allowed to vote on it.
why.C: A charter is an official document granting rights or setting out rules, so it is the paper rather than the right to vote itself.
why.D: Prestige means respect and high standing in other people's eyes, which is not something you exercise at a ballot box.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: One ______ of the contract requires payment within thirty days.
items.explanation: A term here is one condition of a contract, which is what requires payment within thirty days; a trace, capital and volume are not conditions.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A trace is a small remaining sign that something was once there, not a rule written into an agreement.
why.C: Capital has more than one meaning — a country's main city, a big letter at the start of a name — and none of those is a condition written into a contract.
why.D: A volume is one book of a set, or an amount, or loudness, and none of those is a rule about paying within thirty days.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Scientists tried to ______ the contamination back to its source.
items.explanation: To trace is to follow something back to its source, which is exactly what the scientists tried to do; you cannot grant, cultivate or render contamination.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To grant is to give or allow something officially, and nobody hands out contamination.
why.B: To cultivate is to grow something or carefully build it up, like a crop or a friendship — the scientists wanted to follow the contamination back, not raise it.
why.C: Render means to make something become a certain way, as in rendering a room unusable, which is not a word for following a trail backwards.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Her ______ reply arrived within five minutes.
items.explanation: Prompt means quick, without delay, which is what a reply arriving within five minutes is; rigid, remote and static describe something else.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Rigid means stiff and unbending, and a reply could be rigid in tone and still take a week to arrive.
why.C: Remote means far away or out of the way, which is about distance, not about how quickly something came.
why.D: Static is about whether a thing changes at all, which says nothing about a reply arriving in five minutes.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Play was ______ until the rain stopped.
items.explanation: To suspend something is to halt it for a time, and play waits here until the rain stops.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To grant is to give or allow something officially, so granted play would be permitted play — but the sentence needs a word for play stopping while the rain falls.
why.B: To decline is to refuse something politely, or to go downhill, and you can refuse an invitation but not refuse play until the rain stops.
why.D: To evoke is to bring a feeling or a memory to mind, the way a smell can evoke a kitchen, so it is not a word for halting a game.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Beth was ______ with the simple meal and asked for nothing more.
items.explanation: Content here means satisfied, which is what asking for nothing more shows; static, capital and literal are not feelings.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Static is used of things rather than of feelings, so it is not a word for how Beth feels about her meal.
why.B: None of capital's meanings — a country's main city, a big letter at the start of a name — is a way of feeling about a meal.
why.D: Literal means taking words exactly as they are, with no figure of speech, so a person can be literal-minded but cannot be literal with a meal.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The company needed more ______ to expand its business.
items.explanation: Capital here means money to invest, which is what expanding a business needs; content, volume and a term are not money.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Content means satisfied, or else the things inside something, and being satisfied is not what a company needs in order to grow.
why.C: Volume means an amount, or loudness, or one book of a set, so it names a quantity of something rather than what pays for an expansion.
why.D: A term is one condition of an agreement, or a stretch of time like a school term, and neither is something a company needs more of to expand.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: STATIC most nearly means:
items.explanation: static: not changing, motionless — The population remained static for several years.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Expensive means costing a lot of money, and static is about whether a thing changes, not what it costs.
why.C: Very social describes a person who loves company, and static is not about people at all.
why.D: Changing rapidly is the exact opposite of static, because something static stays as it is.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: To SUSPECT something means to:
items.explanation: suspect: to think it may be true without being sure — She suspected the door had been left open. Said SUS-pect, it is a noun: the person thought to have done it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Proving something false means showing for certain that it is not so, while suspecting is having a hunch with no proof either way.
why.C: Knowing something for certain means being sure, and suspecting is the step before that, when you think it may be true but cannot yet show it.
why.D: Forgetting about something is putting it out of your mind, whereas when you suspect something it is very much on your mind.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Even after the first three attempts failed, she stayed ______ and tried once more.
items.explanation: Resolute means determined and unwavering, and she tried once more after three failures.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hesitant means holding back, unsure whether to go on, but she tried once more, which is the opposite of hanging back.
why.B: Careless means not taking care or attention, and the sentence says she failed three times, not that she was sloppy about it.
why.D: Distant means far away, or cool and unfriendly, and neither one describes someone who keeps trying.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DUBIOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: dubious: doubtful, unsure, suspicious about something — Jo was dubious about Amy's plan to bake a cake all by herself.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Loyal means faithful and sticking by someone, which is about who you stand with rather than whether you believe something.
why.B: Cheerful means happy and in good spirits, which has nothing to do with being dubious — that is about having doubts.
why.C: Certain means being completely sure, which is the opposite of dubious — someone dubious has doubts.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The campaign set out to ______ the disease completely, leaving none of it behind.
items.explanation: To eradicate something is to wipe it out entirely, and the campaign leaves none of the disease behind.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To suspend something is to stop it for a time, and anything stopped for a time can start again, while the campaign wanted none of the disease left at all.
why.B: To evoke is to bring a feeling or a memory to mind, the way a song can evoke a summer, so it is not a word for getting rid of something.
why.C: To grant is to give or allow something officially, and a disease is not something anyone hands out.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: CONSPICUOUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: conspicuous: noticeable, obvious, easy to pick out — Jo's bright red hair was conspicuous among the other girls.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Ordinary means usual and nothing special, so an ordinary thing blends in, while a conspicuous one stands out.
why.C: Quiet means making little sound, and something can be completely silent and still be impossible to miss, like a bright red coat.
why.D: Hidden means out of sight, which is the opposite of conspicuous — you spot a conspicuous thing straight away.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DISCRETION most nearly means:
items.explanation: discretion: good judgment about what to say and when — Jo used great discretion when sharing her stories, never revealing which sisters they were about.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Wealth means having a great deal of money, and discretion costs nothing; it is about knowing what to say and when.
why.C: Speed is how fast something happens, and discretion is often the opposite, taking a moment before you speak.
why.D: Loud disagreement is the opposite of discretion — discretion is the quiet good sense to know what to say and when to say nothing.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: RETALIATE most nearly means:
items.explanation: retaliate: respond with revenge, strike back — When Amy burned Jo's manuscript, Jo wanted to retaliate.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Remembering fondly means looking back on something warmly, which is closer to the word reminisce, while retaliating is hitting back.
why.C: Retreat means to back away or withdraw, which is the opposite of striking back; the two words only look alike because both begin with re-.
why.D: Repair means to mend something that is broken, and retaliating usually leaves things worse rather than mended.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: He had to ______ a yawn in the middle of the long speech.
items.explanation: To stifle something is to hold it back or smother it, which is what he does with the yawn.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Unite means to join together into one, which is something people or groups do, not something you do to a yawn.
why.C: Retrieve means to fetch something back, the way a dog retrieves a ball, and he needed to hold the yawn in, not go and get it.
why.D: Cultivate means to grow or carefully build something up, and encouraging the yawn was the last thing he wanted.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SUBSEQUENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: subsequent: following later, coming after — The first meeting was short; subsequent ones ran for hours.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Motionless means not moving at all, which is about movement, while subsequent is about when something happens.
why.C: Not yet decided describes something still up in the air, closer to a word like pending, while subsequent simply means later.
why.D: Happening before is the opposite of subsequent, because subsequent events are the ones that come after.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SUPERIOR most nearly means:
items.explanation: superior: better or higher-ranking than something else — The second draft was superior in every way.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Lasting only briefly describes something temporary, like a passing shower; superior is about rank or quality, and says nothing about how long a thing lasts.
why.C: Equal means the same as something else, level with it — but superior means above it, better or higher in rank.
why.D: Below others in rank is what inferior means, and it is superior's opposite: the super- in superior points upwards.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: SUPPLEMENT most nearly means:
items.explanation: supplement: add to or complete something that is not quite enough — She supplemented her notes with diagrams from the library book.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To hide something is to keep it out of sight, while to supplement it is to add something extra to what is already there.
why.B: To argue against something is to speak in opposition to it; supplementing it is helping it along by adding more.
why.D: Taking away entirely is the opposite of supplementing — a supplement adds to what is not quite enough, it never removes it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The evidence was too ______ to ignore; everyone could see the broken window.
items.explanation: Tangible means solid and plain to see or touch, which a broken window everyone can see is; whimsical, subjective and remote describe evidence you cannot point at.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Whimsical means playful and fanciful, the way a made-up story is — but a broken window that everyone can see is solid and real.
why.B: Subjective means a matter of what someone believes rather than of what is there, and a broken window is there for anyone to look at.
why.C: Remote means far away or distant, and a broken window everyone can see is as close and as plain as evidence gets.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The hikers sought ______ in a cabin when the storm became dangerous.
items.explanation: A sanctuary is a place of safety, which is what a cabin becomes when a storm turns dangerous; consensus, volume and prestige are not shelters.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A consensus is a meeting of minds among a group, not a place — and what the hikers needed from the storm was somewhere safe to be.
why.B: Volume means how loud a sound is, or how much space something fills — neither is a thing you can shelter inside.
why.C: Prestige means the respect and admiration a person or place has earned, which does not keep anybody out of a storm.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The witness gave a ______ account that contradicted the earlier statement.
items.explanation: Conflicting accounts disagree with each other, which is what contradicting the earlier statement means; prompt, unanimous and stationary do not describe a clash.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Prompt means quick and without delay, but this sentence is about an account that disagrees with the earlier one, not about how fast it arrived.
why.B: Unanimous means agreed on by everybody, which is the opposite of an account that contradicts what was said before.
why.D: Stationary means staying in one place, which is about where a thing is, not about whether two accounts match.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The doctor tried to ______ the worried child with a calm voice.
items.explanation: To soothe is to calm someone, which is what a calm voice is for; to stifle, suspect or trace a worried child is not to comfort them.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To stifle something is to smother it or hold it back, so stifling a worried child would mean keeping her quiet rather than calming her down.
why.B: To suspect someone is to think they may have done something wrong, which is not what a doctor does with a calm voice.
why.D: To trace is to follow something's path, or to draw over its lines, and neither is a way of comforting anybody.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A ______ student keeps working carefully even when a task is difficult.
items.explanation: Diligent means carefully hardworking, which is what keeping at a difficult task shows; static, reckless and aloof are the opposite.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Static means making no progress and going nowhere, so a static student would be one who never gets any further — not one who keeps at a hard task.
why.C: Reckless means charging ahead without thinking about the danger, and this student is working carefully at something hard.
why.D: Aloof means keeping apart from other people and staying distant from them, which says nothing about how hard somebody works.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The model ship took months of ______ work, with every tiny rope tied by hand.
items.explanation: Painstaking means done with great care and attention to every detail, which is what tying every tiny rope by hand takes.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Hasty means done in a hurry, and work that takes months with every rope tied by hand is the opposite of hurried.
why.C: Careless means not taking care or attention, but tying every tiny rope by hand takes a great deal of care.
why.D: Brief means lasting only a short time, and this work took months.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A referee has to stay ______ and judge only what actually happened.
items.explanation: Objective means going by facts that can be checked rather than by feelings, and a referee judges only what actually happened.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Subjective means coming from inside one person's own head rather than from what actually happened, which is exactly what a referee must not do.
why.B: Feisty means lively and quick to fight back, which may be spirited but is not what keeps a referee fair.
why.D: Tangible means solid enough to touch or point at, which describes things themselves, not the way a person judges them.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Which flavour tastes best is ______, because it depends on who you ask.
items.explanation: Subjective means resting on personal opinion rather than on checkable fact, and this depends on who you ask.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Unanimous means everyone agreeing, but here people disagree — that is why it depends on who you ask.
why.B: Stationary is about a thing not budging from where it is, which has nothing to do with opinions about flavour.
why.C: Objective means going by what is actually so rather than by how you feel about it, and how a flavour tastes is only ever how it strikes you.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The exercise bike stays ______ however hard its wheels are turning.
items.explanation: Stationary means staying in one place, which the bike does even while its wheels spin.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Frequent means happening often, which is about how often something occurs, not about whether it stays in one place.
why.C: Unsteady means wobbly and likely to tip over, and nothing in the sentence says the bike wobbles at all.
why.D: Distant means far away from something else, and nothing here puts the bike far from anything — its wheels turn hard while it goes nowhere.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Despite the storm, the bridge remained ______ and safe to cross.
items.explanation: Stable means steady and safe to rely on, which is what a bridge that came through the storm is; static means unchanging, stationary means not moving, remote means far off.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Static means unchanging, and a thing can be perfectly unchanging and still not be safe — the sentence is praising the bridge for holding firm.
why.C: A stationary thing is one that never travels anywhere, which every bridge manages, storm or no storm; the point here is that it is still firm enough to cross.
why.D: Remote means far away, and the sentence is about the bridge surviving the storm, not about where it stands.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The frozen image on the monitor was ______ for several seconds.
items.explanation: Static means not changing, which is what a frozen image on a monitor is; social, prompt and spacious describe nothing about a frozen screen.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Social means having to do with being among other people, which a frozen picture on a screen has nothing to do with.
why.B: Prompt means quick and on time, but this image was stuck for several seconds, which is the opposite of quick.
why.D: Spacious means having plenty of room inside, which describes a room or a bag, not a picture that has stopped changing.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The watchmaker examined the ______ gears, each tiny part fitting precisely.
items.explanation: Intricate means made of many small parts fitting together, which is what tiny gears meshing precisely are; subjective, literal and remote say nothing about detail.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Subjective means based on someone's personal opinion, but gears are real parts, and the sentence is describing how detailed they are.
why.B: Literal means taking words exactly as they are said, with no figurative meaning behind them — it describes language, not gears.
why.D: Remote means far away, and the watchmaker had these gears right in front of him.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The committee reached a ______ after everyone finally agreed.
items.explanation: A consensus is agreement reached by everyone, which is what “everyone finally agreed” says; volume, prejudice and a trace are not agreements.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Volume means how loud something is, or how much space it fills, and neither is a thing a committee can reach.
why.B: Prejudice means an unfair opinion formed before you know the facts, which is not what a group arrives at when everyone finally agrees.
why.C: A trace is a tiny leftover sign that something was once there, not an agreement.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The report tried to remain ______ by relying on measurable facts.
items.explanation: Objective means based on facts rather than opinion, which is what relying on measurable facts is; conspicuous, rigid and literal are not the opposite of opinionated.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: Conspicuous means standing out so that it is easy to notice, which is about being seen, not about sticking to the facts.
why.C: Rigid means stiff and unbending, like a metal bar or a strict rule, and a report built on measurable facts is meant to be fair rather than stiff.
why.D: Literal means keeping to the exact words rather than a figurative meaning — a report can be perfectly literal and still be full of opinion.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: In 'a remote possibility,' REMOTE means:
items.explanation: remote: unlikely, barely possible — a remote possibility is one you would not bet on. Its everyday meaning is far away, and a distant chance is where this use comes from.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Remote can make a place sound lonely, but the word itself means far off — a remote possibility is far from likely, not dangerous.
why.C: Formal means proper and done by the rules, which is no part of what remote means.
why.D: Nearby is remote turned round the other way: remote means far away, and a remote possibility is a long way from happening.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The camera's ______ design made it easy to carry.
items.explanation: Compact means small and neatly packed, which is what makes a camera easy to carry; remote, tender and domestic say nothing about size.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Remote means far away, so it tells you where something is rather than how small and neatly packed it is.
why.C: Tender means gentle and soft-hearted, or sore when it is touched, and neither has anything to do with carrying a camera.
why.D: Domestic means to do with the home, or with your own country rather than abroad — not with how big a thing is.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: GRANT most nearly means:
items.explanation: grant: to give or allow something — the opposite of refusing it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.B: To refuse is to say no, which is the exact opposite of granting something.
why.C: To borrow is to take something for a while and give it back, while to grant is to give it or to give permission for it.
why.D: To delay is to put something off until later, but granting it means saying yes to it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: EXPLOIT most nearly means:
items.explanation: exploit: to take advantage of someone or something, often unfairly.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To repair something is to fix what is broken, while to exploit it is to use it for your own gain, often unfairly.
why.C: To praise someone is to say good things about them; exploiting them is using them for what you can get out of them.
why.D: To ignore something is to pay it no attention at all, but exploiting it means making full use of it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: DECLINE most nearly means:
items.explanation: decline: to refuse or turn something down — the opposite of accepting it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To repeat is to do or say something over again, which has nothing to do with turning an offer down.
why.B: To enlarge is to make something bigger — and decline, in its other meaning, is about getting smaller or weaker, which is nearer the opposite.
why.C: To accept is to say yes, and to decline is to say no, so this is the other way round.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A few notes of that song can ______ a whole summer she had forgotten.
items.explanation: To evoke something is to bring it to mind, and the notes call the summer back.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To measure something is to find out how big or how long it is, but the notes are bringing a memory back, not sizing it up.
why.B: To postpone something is to put it off until later, and a summer already gone cannot be put off — only called back to mind.
why.D: To destroy something is to wreck it, and the notes bring the forgotten summer back rather than ruining it.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: Early warnings helped ______ a larger disaster.
items.explanation: To avert is to prevent something bad before it happens, which is what early warnings do; to provoke, inundate or dwindle a disaster is not to stop it.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To provoke is to stir something up on purpose, which is the opposite of what early warnings are meant to do.
why.B: To inundate is to flood or swamp something with far too much of it, so you could be inundated by a disaster but not inundate one.
why.C: To dwindle is to shrink away little by little, and it is something that happens on its own — you cannot dwindle a disaster.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: The agency decided to ______ the license after repeated violations.
items.explanation: To revoke is to cancel something already granted, which is what repeated violations cost a license; to proclaim, acquire or commend it is not to take it away.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: To proclaim is to announce something publicly, which is not what happens to a license after repeated violations.
why.B: To acquire is to get something for yourself, but here the agency is taking the license away rather than gaining one.
why.C: To commend is to praise someone for doing well, and repeated violations do not earn praise.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: A UTOPIA is:
items.explanation: utopia: an imagined perfect society — a place arranged so well that nothing goes wrong. Its opposite, where everything has gone wrong, is a dystopia.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: A legal decision is a ruling handed down by a court, and utopia is not a law word at all — it names an imagined place.
why.C: A utopia is imagined as a place where everything has been arranged perfectly, so nothing about it is dangerous.
why.D: A rural village is a small settlement out in the countryside; a utopia may be any size, and what makes it one is that it is imagined to be perfect.

items.subject: VR
items.prompt: TREACHEROUS most nearly means:
items.explanation: treacherous: dangerous or untrustworthy; an icy path and a false friend are both treacherous — The mountain track was treacherous after the storm.
items.source: Original content authored for Sheila ISEE

why.A: Ordinary means usual and nothing out of the common way, but treacherous marks a thing out as dangerous or not to be trusted.
why.C: Safe and dependable is treacherous turned right around — a treacherous path, or a treacherous friend, is exactly the one you cannot rely on.
why.D: Quiet is about how much noise a thing makes, and something treacherous can be perfectly quiet while still being dangerous.
